headline: High risk of prompt-injection, data leakage, and cascading errors: gpt-engineer writes/reads project files while ComfyUI exposes model/workflow files and can be driven by user content.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: ComfyUI can ingest workflows/files and gpt-engineer reads and writes the project directory, so attacker-controlled content can cross from one agent to the other through shared files. No MCP or clipboard bridge is shown, but the shared filesystem path is enough for instruction-like payloads to be misread as trusted input.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same project directory or model/workflow folder
IF gpt-engineer parses ComfyUI-generated text or files as instructions without sanitization
mitigations: Use separate directories for workflows and code
Rename or quarantine untrusted files before gpt-engineer reads them
Add a manual review step for any file passed from ComfyUI to gpt-engineer
requires-engineering: add provenance tags to shared files

B_data_leakage.rationale: ComfyUI touches images, videos, audio, seeds, and model artifacts, while gpt-engineer reads the project directory and can send prompts to a configured model backend. If sensitive assets are placed in the shared workspace, gpt-engineer can expose them through its inference calls or generated outputs. The pair lacks explicit isolation, so leakage is plausible in default project workflows.
conditions: IF sensitive images, seeds, or checkpoints are stored in the same project directory used by gpt-engineer
IF gpt-engineer forwards file contents into its model backend
mitigations: Keep sensitive media outside the shared project directory
Restrict gpt-engineer inputs to redacted manifests
Disable uploading of file contents where possible
Review generated outputs before sharing externally
requires-engineering: enforce workspace-level access controls

C_capability_conflict.rationale: ComfyUI is offline and does not write files, but gpt-engineer has write_filesystem and per-project shared state via the project directory. That creates overlapping mutable access to the same workspace, so concurrent edits can clobber workflows or generated code even without git writes. The conflict is real in default project setups, though not as severe as unrestricted dual-write systems.
conditions: IF both agents operate on the same project directory
IF ComfyUI workflow files and gpt-engineer output files are edited concurrently
mitigations: Assign separate subdirectories per agent
Serialize writes with a simple operator checklist
Back up the project directory before each run
Use file naming conventions to avoid collisions
requires-engineering: add locking around shared workspace writes

D_cascading_error.rationale: gpt-engineer can act on generated code and ComfyUI can emit workflows/assets that may be treated as authoritative inputs. If gpt-engineer consumes ComfyUI output without verification, errors or malicious content can cascade into generated code or executed actions. Because gpt-engineer can execute generated code with the user's privileges, the blast radius can be irreversible.
conditions: IF gpt-engineer uses ComfyUI-produced files as trusted specifications
IF the operator enables execution of generated code
mitigations: Require manual review of ComfyUI outputs before code generation
Do not execute generated code automatically
Use a diff-only review step for generated files
Keep a rollback backup of the project directory
requires-engineering: add validation between image/workflow outputs and code actions

E_compliance.rationale: No explicit residency, certification, or retention mismatch is documented for either agent, so a compliance breach is not established. However, gpt-engineer handles an API key and writes project files while ComfyUI stores model artifacts locally, so compliance gaps could arise if regulated data is placed in the shared workspace. The evidence is weaker here than for the operational risks.
conditions: IF regulated data is stored in the shared project directory
IF the operator routes sensitive prompts or artifacts through gpt-engineer
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of the shared workspace
Document what data classes each agent may touch
Rotate any exposed API keys immediately after testing
Review retention settings for the model backend
requires-engineering: add policy enforcement for regulated data
